sanskrit_verse: विक्रीय पण्यं मूल्येन क्रेतुर्यो न प्रयच्छति । स्थावरस्य क्षयं दाप्यो जङ्गमस्य क्रियाफलम् ॥
transliteration: vikrīya paṇyaṁ mūlyena kretur yo na prayacchati | sthāvarasya kṣayaṁ dāpyo jaṅgamasya kriyāphalam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who sells a commodity and does not deliver it upon receiving payment shall compensate for the loss of immovable property and bear the consequence of action regarding movable property.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from fulfillment of transactional duty
Causation arises through failure to complete exchange
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by possession and intent
Restoration logic demands equivalence in value and form
Consciousness alignment requires integrity in commercial engagement
executable_legal_axioms: IF seller receives payment AND fails to deliver goods THEN seller incurs liability equal to item's current market value OR replacement cost
IF undelivered item is immovable THEN compensation includes depreciation and opportunity loss
IF undelivered item is movable THEN enforce completion of transaction OR return of full payment plus consequential damages
NO punitive interest or penalty SHALL apply; restoration only aligns with Dharma
supreme_court_application: In commercial disputes involving non-delivery post-payment, the Supreme Court shall determine liability based on asset classification—immovable or movable—and mandate immediate restitution without punitive measures. The threshold of responsibility lies in proof of transaction completion failure, not intent malice.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that non-delivery breaches contractual Dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential causality: receipt of payment → obligation to deliver → failure → liability. Responsibility is proportional to capacity to perform. No punitive element enters, as justice serves realignment, not vengeance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Mandatory delivery of equivalent product within seven days
Full refund with additional value adjustment if delivery impossible
Public registry entry to ensure transparency and prevent repetition
Seller undergoes commercial conduct rectification process under spiritual oversight
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: transactions bind not by contract alone but by consciousness of duty. Dharma prevails where commerce reflects truth. Reality remains non-punitive, guided solely by the awakened conscience of the actor.
